mcp_peer._note: The opponent is our protocol partner, not a metered third-party API. The gatekeeper exists to be a good citizen towards Anthropic and Gmail; applying those limits here only risks delaying our own reply past the opponent's 30s deadline and forfeiting a game to our own throttle. Rate raised so it never shapes a legitimate match; concurrency stays at the Appendix F ceiling of 2.

anthropic._note: max_retries 1: a hint is optional and has a zero-token template floor beneath it, but the 30 s turn deadline is not optional. At the shared default of 3 retries 5 s apart, two unreachable vendors cost 20 s on the first hint of a match — measured — which is most of the deadline. retry_after_seconds stays at the Appendix F minimum because it is never reached: the gatekeeper only sleeps between attempts.

inbound_peer._note: INBOUND messages from the opponent. This is a flood backstop, not a throttle on play: the real protection against a peer filling memory is the bounded inbox queue, which refuses politely and does not grow. The ceiling was 120/min on the assumption that turns are human-paced; they are not — a turn costs us milliseconds, so two fast peers exceed 2/sec trivially. In a six-game rehearsal against the reference we rejected its legitimate turn mid-game, then timed out waiting for the message we had thrown away ourselves. Set far above anything honest play can reach.
